skill.name: w-docs
skill.description: Guides an AI assistant to update the correct documentation layer for code, feature, setup, and workflow changes.
skill.summary: Keep technical documentation aligned with current code and project conventions.
skill.author: blockmatic

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks in SKILL.md, not Ruby or shell execution. No semantic security findings or prompt injection attempts were identified.

static_findings.snippet: | Technical docs (path in `AGENTS.md`) | Architecture, ADRs, how-to | Behavior, architecture, comman
Inline comments only when the code is otherwise misleading. Do not copy MDX into rules or READMEs. D

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on line 13 are Markdown code formatting around AGENTS.md, not Ruby or shell execution. The line contains documentation guidance and no executable command.
The backticks on line 17 format the @ character in Markdown prose, not a command expression. The line provides documentation rules and contains no executable code.

content.value_statement: Documentation updates often land in the wrong file or duplicate existing information. This skill directs the assistant to the owning documentation layer and keeps project guidance consistent.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the documentation layer that owns a code or feature change.
Finds an existing documentation section or topic page before creating content.
Updates MDX when canonical technical explanations change.
Updates README files for setup, scripts, and package purpose changes.
Updates agent rules when a project constraint changes.
Proposes grouped file moves without performing them unless requested.
limitations: Requires repository-specific documentation rules and paths to be available.
Does not inspect undocumented product requirements or infer missing architecture.
Does not commit changes unless the user explicitly requests a commit.
Does not move files without an explicit implementation request and path.

use_cases.title: Keep feature documentation current
use_cases.description: Update the canonical MDX topic when a feature changes behavior, architecture, commands, conventions, or workflow.

use_cases.title: Maintain setup instructions
use_cases.description: Patch the nearest README when scripts, setup steps, or package purpose change, and link to deeper technical documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan documentation moves
use_cases.description: Produce a concise grouped from-and-to list for related documentation moves when the user provides a destination path.

prompt_templates.title: Document a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Document this change in the repository. Find the owning documentation page, update only the necessary section, and show the files changed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a focused code change.

prompt_templates.title: Update feature guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current feature behavior and update the existing MDX topic. Preserve the repository structure, avoid duplicate pages, and include relevant commands.

prompt_templates.title: Align setup documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Update documentation for these script and setup changes: [describe changes]. Patch the nearest README for run instructions and link to the canonical technical details.
prompt_templates.scenario: README and technical documentation need coordinated updates.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a documentation move
prompt_templates.prompt: Given the documentation move request and destination path below, propose the smallest grouped from-and-to list. Do not move files or commit changes. Request: [details]. Destination: [path].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a documentation restructure.

output_examples.input: A command changed in the package setup process.
output_examples.output: Updated the nearest README with the new command and linked the existing technical documentation page.

output_examples.input: A feature behavior and its workflow changed.
output: Updated the existing MDX topic with the new behavior.
Added the changed workflow and command details.
Left agent rules unchanged because no constraint changed.

output_examples.input: Move related documentation into the provided architecture directory.
output_examples.output: Proposed a grouped from-and-to file list and did not move files because implementation was not requested.

best_practices: Start with the repository rules and locate the documentation layer that owns the change.
Reuse an existing topic page before creating a new documentation page.
Keep README content focused on setup and link to canonical technical explanations.
anti_patterns: Creating a second sitemap when the repository already has a durable information architecture.
Copying MDX content into agent rules or README files.
Moving files or committing changes without an explicit user request.

faq.question: What does this skill document?
faq.answer: It documents current code or feature behavior in the repository layer that owns the explanation.

faq.question: Does it create new pages?
faq.answer: It creates a page only when no existing topic page fits the required explanation.

faq.question: When should it update a README?
faq.answer: It updates the nearest README for setup, scripts, or package purpose changes.

faq.question: Does it update agent rules?
faq.answer: It updates agent rules only when a project constraint has changed.

faq.question: Does it move files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It proposes a grouped move list and saves it only when the user provides a path.

faq.question: Does it commit documentation changes?
faq.answer: No. It does not commit unless the user explicitly requests a commit.
